analysis: Examined docs/developer/build.md (head lines 1-1090) and the metadata and truncated patch excerpt for scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py. The changed ranges in build.md are the date stamp (line 3), the Darkbloom Sandbox cache wording (573-576), a new CI-cache gating paragraph (658-680), the restored-.git validation description (724-730) and a flowchart node (757). All of these are documentation of CI behavior. The test script change adds a stricter VALIDATE_GIT shell check and a CACHE_GATE_STEP check. VALIDATE_GIT rejects a restored .git that is a symlink, holds hooks or symlinks, or sets core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or includes. The CACHE_GATE_STEP check asserts that every cache step is skipped on a Darkbloom runner with no Darkbloom cache. Both are defensive hardening of CI cache poisoning and cross-scope cache write. Neither touches the provider runtime, the WebSocket contract, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, the prefix cache (T-041), the fan helper or the add-on boundaries. No threat-model assets or trust boundaries are weakened. The docs state that CI (master) restores only the strict first cache tier, so releasable builds do not reuse objects from another recipe, which is consistent with the existing release-integrity posture. Coverage limits: the actual workflow and action YAML (provider-tests.yml, provider-ci-build/action.yml, ci-master.yml) and the full script patch were not supplied. The claims that every cache step is gated and every routed job sets CI_ACTIONS_CACHE first are therefore unverified against the YAML. They are CI supply-chain matters outside the provider threat-model scope and not provider-runtime regressions. No findings.
